title: Hemp seeds: protein, fat, omega-3, and nutrition

seo.title: Hemp seeds: protein, fat, magnesium, and omega-3
seo.meta_description: Hulled hemp seeds provide about 553 calories, 31.6 g protein, 48.8 g fat, and ~700 mg magnesium per 100 g. A 1-ounce serving gives a more useful picture.
seo.search_intent: Understand the nutrition of hulled hemp hearts, including protein, fat, ALA omega-3, minerals, calories, and realistic serving size.

excerpt: Hulled hemp is highly concentrated: about 31–32 g protein and 49 g fat per 100 g. One ounce provides roughly 9 g protein, 155 calories, ALA omega-3, and a substantial amount of magnesium.
content_html:
Hulled hemp seeds, often sold as hemp hearts, are usually marketed for protein. Protein is only part of the picture. They are a concentrated combination of protein, polyunsaturated fat, magnesium, zinc, and plant omega-3.

What hemp hearts provide

NutrientPer 100 gPer 1 oz (28 g)
Calories~553 kcal~155 kcal
Protein~31.6 g~8.8 g
Fat~48.8 g~13.7 g
Fiber~4 g~1.1 g
Magnesium~700 mg~196 mg
Zinc~9.9 mg~2.8 mg

These numbers refer to hulled seed. Whole hemp seed retains a fibrous outer shell and can show a different nutrient profile.

About 32% protein by weight

At about 31.6 g protein per 100 g, hemp hearts are slightly above many pumpkin-seed references near 30 g and much higher than seeds valued primarily for fiber.

The serving-size reality is different: one ounce provides about 9 g protein. Reaching 30 g protein from hemp alone would require close to 95 g and more than 500 calories.

Most of the fat is unsaturated

About 49 g fat per 100 g explains much of hemp’s calorie density. Most of that fat is polyunsaturated, including both linoleic acid, an omega-6 fat, and ALA, an omega-3 fat.

ALA can be around 8–9 g per 100 g, so one ounce may provide roughly 2.2–2.5 g. That is meaningful but below the concentration in flax and chia.

Plant ALA is not equivalent to fish EPA and DHA

The omega-3 in hemp is primarily ALA. NIH notes that the body converts ALA to EPA and DHA only in limited amounts. Therefore, 2.4 g ALA from hemp should not be described as if it were 2.4 g EPA+DHA from fish.

Magnesium is exceptionally concentrated

A USDA-derived reference for hulled hemp is around 700 mg magnesium per 100 g. One ounce is therefore roughly 196 mg. The same serving also provides around 2.8 mg zinc, along with phosphorus, iron, copper, and manganese.

Is hemp a “complete protein”?

Hemp contains all indispensable amino acids, but protein quality is not a yes-or-no question based only on whether each amino acid is present. Their proportions and digestibility matter too.

In a varied diet, hemp works particularly well as an addition to oatmeal, yogurt, salads, or smoothies where it adds protein and minerals without needing to be the only protein source.

The useful takeaway

Hemp hearts are unusually protein-rich for a seed, but they are also calorie-dense. A one-ounce serving provides about 9 g protein, unsaturated fats, ALA, and a large amount of magnesium. That serving tells a more practical story than the impressive per-100-g numbers alone.

faq.question: How much protein is in hemp seeds?
faq.answer: Hulled hemp seeds provide about 31–32 g per 100 g, or about 9 g per ounce.

faq.question: Do hemp seeds contain omega-3?
faq.answer: Yes, mainly ALA. One ounce can provide roughly 2.2–2.5 g depending on the reference.
